subChunks.title: Aspect Ratio and Media Handling
subChunks.hookHtml: Images, videos, and embeds have their own natural dimensions that can break your layout if not constrained. Tailwind's aspect ratio utilities lock an element's proportions regardless of its content's natural size — essential for image grids, video embeds, and media cards where consistent sizing matters.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Aspect ratio utilities

aspect-auto       /* natural aspect ratio */
aspect-square     /* 1:1 (width = height) */
aspect-video      /* 16:9 (standard video) */
aspect-[4/3]      /* custom: 4:3 ratio */
aspect-[3/2]      /* custom: 3:2 photo ratio */

The image card pattern

<div class="overflow-hidden rounded-xl">
  <div class="aspect-video overflow-hidden">
    <img class="w-full h-full object-cover
               hover:scale-105 transition-transform duration-300"
         src="..." alt="" />
  </div>
  <div class="p-4">content</div>
</div>

Key insight: aspect-video on the container locks the space; w-full h-full object-cover on the image fills it completely, cropping as needed.

Responsive video embed

<div class="aspect-video w-full">
  <iframe
    class="w-full h-full"
    src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/..."
    allowfullscreen
  ></iframe>
</div>

object-fit utilities

object-cover     /* scale to fill, crop excess — most common for images */
object-contain   /* scale to fit, leave letterbox — for logos/icons */
object-fill      /* stretch to fill — distorts aspect ratio */
object-none      /* no scaling — shows at natural size */
object-scale-down /* smallest of contain or none */

/* Position the crop */
object-center    /* centre the crop point (default) */
object-top       /* crop from the top */
object-bottom    /* crop from the bottom */
object-left      /* crop from the left */

Image grid with uniform sizing

<div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-2">
  <div class="aspect-square overflow-hidden rounded-lg">
    <img class="w-full h-full object-cover" src="..." />
  </div>
  <!-- repeat for all items -->
</div>

Avatar sizing

/* Fixed sizes — always equal width and height */
w-6 h-6    /* 24px — tiny (in badges) */
w-8 h-8    /* 32px — small (nav) */
w-10 h-10  /* 40px — medium (list items) */
w-12 h-12  /* 48px — large (profile headers) */
w-16 h-16  /* 64px — XL (hero profiles) */

/* Always pair with object-cover and rounded-full */
<img class="w-10 h-10 rounded-full object-cover" />

Lazy loading images

<img
  class="w-full h-full object-cover"
  src="..."
  alt=""
  loading="lazy"    /* native browser lazy loading */
  decoding="async"  /* decode off the main thread */
/>

Sable: "object-cover is almost always what you want for images in cards and grids — it fills the space and crops intelligently. object-contain is for logos and icons where showing the whole image matters more than filling the space. object-fill stretches and distorts — avoid it for photography."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: An image without constraints is a layout time bomb. It arrives at whatever size the server sends it — 400px, 2000px, portrait, landscape — and breaks your grid. aspect-video on the container, w-full h-full object-cover on the image: these two decisions make every image fit perfectly, regardless of its natural dimensions.

storyBeats.speaker: Responsive image card
storyBeats.text: Slay the Dragon

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a photo gallery grid and a video embed:

  • .gallery-grid: grid, grid-cols-3, gap-2
  • .gallery-item: aspect-square, overflow-hidden, rounded-lg
  • .gallery-img: w-full, h-full, object-cover, hover:scale-110, transition-transform, duration-300
  • .video-embed: aspect-video, w-full, rounded-xl, overflow-hidden, bg-gray-900
  • .avatar-lg: w-16, h-16, rounded-full, object-cover
  • .avatar-md: w-10, h-10, rounded-full, object-cover

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between object-cover and object-contain — when would you use each and what happens to the image in each case? Walk through the pattern for a responsive image that fills a fixed aspect ratio container — why does the container need the aspect-ratio class AND the image need w-full h-full object-cover?

questions.prompt: Which class combination creates a 16:9 aspect ratio container that keeps its proportions as the viewport width changes?
questions.explanation: aspect-video applies aspect-ratio: 16/9. w-full makes the element span its container's width. Together, the height is calculated automatically to maintain the 16:9 ratio at any width. This replaces the old padding-top percentage hack.

questions.prompt: A logo image inside a fixed-size container needs to fit entirely within the container without cropping, showing the full logo with empty space on the sides if needed. Which object-fit utility is correct?
questions.explanation: object-contain scales the image to fit entirely within the container, maintaining aspect ratio and leaving empty space (letterbox) if the container's ratio differs from the image's. This is correct for logos where showing the full image is more important than filling the space. object-cover would crop the logo, potentially hiding part of it.

questions.prompt: An image card uses aspect-video on the container and object-cover on the image. Portrait photos (taller than wide) are heavily cropped. Which class on the image changes where the crop occurs to show the top of portrait photos?
options: object-top — positions the visible portion at the top of the image
object-contain — shows the full image without cropping
object-position-top — CSS property not available in Tailwind
crop-top — Tailwind doesn't control crop position
questions.answer: object-top — positions the visible portion at the top of the image
questions.explanation: object-top sets object-position: top, which tells the browser where to anchor the image when cropping occurs with object-cover. For portrait photos where faces are usually at the top, object-top ensures the top portion is visible rather than the centre. Other options: object-bottom, object-left, object-right, and arbitrary values like object-[50%_25%].
